title: Persistent disks, local SSD and snapshots

videos.script: A machine is easy to replace. Its data is not. This lesson is about where the data lives. {{pd}} A persistent disk is not inside the server. It sits on Google's network and outlives the machine. Its speed grows with its size, up to the machine's own limit. {{regional}} A zonal disk lives in one zone. A regional disk writes every block to two zones, and costs twice as much for it. {{hyperdisk}} Hyperdisk sells space, operations and throughput separately. So a fast disk no longer has to be a big one. {{local}} A local SSD is in the host itself. It is very fast, and it empties when the machine stops. Never the only copy. {{snapshots}} Last, snapshots. Each one copies only what changed. A schedule takes them every night, and they cost less than the disk.
